overview: Crosshaul is a three-dimensional logistics puzzle across eight chambers. Select two cargo cubes and trade one world coordinate: height, width or depth. Every exchange moves both partners along a clear route, so reaching one dock can complicate another delivery. Later chambers add obstacles and a fourth cargo, with a limited exchange allowance and unlimited undo.
rules: Dock every cargo at its matching color and symbol before the exchange allowance runs out.
An exchange swaps only the selected world coordinate between two cargoes; their other coordinates stay unchanged.
Both simultaneous routes must clear baffles, stationary cargo and the moving partner. Rejected routes and equal-coordinate commands cost no allowance.
An accepted exchange spends one allowance. Zero remaining exchanges with undocked cargo fails the chamber; undo refunds the exchange and restart restores its initial state.
After all cargoes dock and their slides finish, advance through all eight chambers. An already docked cargo can be moved again to lend a useful coordinate.
controls: Left-click cargo cubes or their list rows; number keys 1–4 also select the two partners.
X / Y / Z select width / height / depth; Space performs the previewed exchange.
Right-drag orbits the camera and the mouse wheel zooms. Camera orbit never changes the world axes.
Backspace undoes and refunds an exchange; R restarts; Enter advances a completed chamber.
H reveals one legal next-move hint; Tab displays rules; F5 / F9 quick-save and quick-load; Esc opens the menu; F toggles fullscreen.

design.rationale: Exchanging one coordinate couples two deliveries: helping one cargo necessarily relocates its partner. The appeal is planning both clear routes and temporarily disturbing a completed dock to lend a useful coordinate. World-aligned movement and route previews make that spatial trade visible while later obstacles and a fourth cargo develop the same rule.
